question.value: How do AGN illumination, outflows, and host-outflow coupling affect the survival, resilience, and properties of PAH molecules in the nuclear and circumnuclear regions of local AGN?

evidence.quote: In this work, we examine the PAH properties in the circumnuclear regions of AGN and the projected direction of AGN-outflows, and compare them to those in star-forming regions and the innermost regions of AGN.
In particular, we examine the PAH survival conditions in the circumnuclear regions of AGN with sources showing different degrees of coupling between its outflow and host galaxy disk.

claims.hypothesis: AGN illumination and feedback affect PAH populations not only in the innermost nuclear region (~75 pc) but also at circumnuclear (~kpc) scales along the outflow direction, especially when outflow-host coupling is strong.
claims.experiment: Map and extract JWST MIRI/MRS spectra in nuclear, outflow, and star-forming regions of three GATOS AGN (NGC 5506, NGC 5728, NGC 7172) with varying outflow-host coupling, fit PAH bands, and compare 11.3/6.2, 11.3/7.7, and 6.2/7.7 µm PAH ratios to theoretical DFT model grids.
claims.result: Nuclear and outflow-projected regions exhibit elevated 11.3/7.7 and 11.3/6.2 µm PAH ratios (higher neutral PAH fraction) matching high [Ne III]/[Ne II] radiation hardness, while unaffected disk/ring star-forming regions match typical star-forming galaxy ratios and 6.2/7.7 µm size ratios remain similar.
claims.finding: AGN illumination and feedback preferentially deplete less resilient ionized PAH molecules (6.2 and 7.7 µm) relative to neutral PAHs (11.3 µm) up to kpc scales without strongly altering molecular sizes.

evidence.quote: By comparing our observations to PAH diagnostic diagrams, we find that, in general, regions located in the projected direction of the AGN-outflow occupy similar positions on the PAH diagnostic diagrams as those of the innermost regions of AGN.

We find that, even in Seyfert-like AGN, illumination and feedback from the AGN might affect the PAH population at kpc scales. In particular, the fraction of ionized PAH molecules is low in the outflow zone compared with that of star-forming regions.

claims.hypothesis: The ratio of PAH emission to warm molecular hydrogen (6.2 µm PAH / H2 0-0 S(1)) can disentangle AGN-dominated (shock/radiation-affected) regions from star-forming activity.
claims.experiment: Compare spatially resolved maps of 6.2 µm PAH / H2 0-0 S(1) against 11.3/6.2 PAH ratios and [Ne III]/[Ne II] radiation hardness across all spaxels in NGC 5506, NGC 5728, and NGC 7172.
claims.result: Spaxels with 6.2 µm PAH / H2 0-0 S(1) < 5 correspond to AGN-dominated regions with high [Ne III]/[Ne II] and elevated 11.3/6.2 PAH ratios, whereas spaxels with > 12 trace star-forming rings and disks.
claims.finding: The PAH-H2 diagnostic effectively separates AGN feedback from star-forming activity at sub-kpc scales.

evidence.quote: In particular, we find that values of the 6.2 µm PAH/H 2 0-0 S(1)>12 correspond to SF-dominated regions, while those regions with 6.2 µm PAH/H 2 0-0 S(1)<5 are AGN-dominated.
Furthermore, PAH bands together with H 2 and low IP emission lines allow to disentangle AGN feedback from star-forming activity.

why_this_data.value: Sub-arcsecond mid-IR JWST/MIRI-MRS spectroscopy (4.9–28.1 µm) probes multiple ionized and neutral PAH bands at ~75 pc to kpc scales in obscured regions, while ALMA CO(3–2) traces the cold molecular gas distribution, and the three targets span weak to strong outflow-host galaxy coupling at similar AGN luminosities and distances.

evidence.quote: Mid-IR subarcsecond angular observations (<0.5 ′′ ) of local AGN (at distances of ∼tens of Mpc) enable us to probe their nuclear/circumnuclear regions (inner ∼100 pc scales).
The targets have been selected to have different degrees of outflowhost galaxy coupling from very strong to weak (see e.g. Fig. 4 in Ramos Almeida et al. 2022).

why_this_method.value: Extracting spectra in larger targeted apertures increases signal-to-noise for faint PAH bands, and a differential extinction model is required for nuclear regions where complex dust continuum and high extinction cause standard PAHFIT to fail.

evidence.quote: Thus, it is unlikely that an evolved stellar population is significantly contributing to the 11.3µm PAH emission observed in our targets.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Outflowing torus, broad spherical-bubble AGN outflows, or beam smearing as explanations for the high-velocity dispersion enhancement perpendicular to the jet in NGC 5728; jet-induced lateral acceleration of gas out of the disc plane is favored due to strong geometrical coupling.

evidence.quote: A number of possibilities could account for this high-velocity dispersion enhancement: (1) Jet-induced acceleration of gas out of the disc plane (e.g. Audibert et al. 2023; Venturi et al. 2021); (2) Outflowing torus (e.g. AlonsoHerrero et al. 2018); (3) Broad AGN-outflows, which might be potentially resembling a spherical bubble.
Given the geometrical coupling of the jet and the host galaxy disk in NGC 5728, the first scenario is most likely, although a detailed kinematic analysis is needed to confirm this.

referee_caveats_inferred: Uncertainties on the measured nuclear and circumnuclear PAH fluxes in Tables A.1 and A.2 are omitted despite Table A.1 caption mentioning 'Fluxes and errors'.

The thresholds separating AGN-dominated (<5) and SF-dominated (>12) spaxels in the 6.2 µm PAH / H2 S(1) diagram rely on visual comparison with [Ne III]/[Ne II] contours rather than a formal physical model.

Different spectral fitting methods are used for the nuclear regions (differential extinction model) versus the circumnuclear apertures (modified PAHFIT), which could introduce systematic offsets in nuclear vs circumnuclear PAH ratios.
